probes.label: help
probes.stdout:
Usage: inspector-cli [options] [target...]

Arguments:
  target                          Command and arguments or URL of the MCP server
                                  (or use --config and --server)

Options:
  --catalog <path>                Writable catalog file (created if missing;
                                  default: ~/.mcp-inspector/mcp.json, or
                                  MCP_CATALOG_PATH)
  --config <path>                 Read-only session config file (served as-is,
                                  never written or seeded; errors if absent)
  --server <name>                 Server name from config/catalog file
  --rename <name>                 New name for the entry (servers/edit only)
  -e <env>                        Environment variables for the server
                                  (KEY=VALUE) (default: {})
  --method <method>               Method to invoke
  --tool-name <toolName>          Tool name (for tools/call method)
  --tool-arg <pairs...>           Tool argument as key=value pair (default: {})
  --uri <uri>                     URI of the resource (resources/read,
                                  resources/directory/read) or of the skill
                                  (skills/get)
  --cursor <cursor>               Opaque pagination cursor (for
                                  resources/directory/read; pass back the
                                  nextCursor from the previous page).
  --prompt-name <promptName>      Name of the prompt (for prompts/get method)
  --prompt-args <pairs...>        Prompt arguments as key=value pairs (default:
                                  {})
  --log-level <level>             Logging level (for logging/setLevel method)
  --cwd <path>                    Working directory for stdio server process
  --transport <type>              Transport type (sse, http, or stdio).
                                  Auto-detected from URL: /mcp → http, /sse →
                                  sse, commands → stdio
  --server-url <url>              Server URL for SSE/HTTP transport
  --header <headers...>           HTTP headers as "HeaderName: Value" pairs (for
                                  HTTP/SSE transports) (default: {})
  --metadata <pairs...>           General metadata as key=value pairs (applied
                                  to all methods) (default: {})
  --tool-metadata <pairs...>      Tool-specific metadata as key=value pairs (for
                                  tools/call method only) (default: {})
  --app-info                      Probe the tool's MCP App UI metadata
                                  (resourceUri, csp, permissions, domain) and
                                  emit it as one JSON line; exit 2 when the tool
                                  has no app. Use with --method tools/call
                                  --tool-name <name> (the tool itself is not
                                  invoked) or --method tools/list (one NDJSON
                                  line per tool).
  --advertise-apps                Advertise the MCP Apps UI extension
                                  (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui) at initialize.
                                  Off by default because the CLI cannot render
                                  an App; set it when a server only exposes its
                                  App tools to a client that claims App support,
                                  e.g. for an --app-info probe.
  --strict                        Report tool-schema portability problems in
                                  full (path, issue, suggested fix) on stderr,
                                  and exit 6 if any is error-severity. Use with
                                  --method tools/list. Without it, a one-line
                                  count is printed instead.
  --verify                        Run the SEP-2640 conformance and digest checks
                                  over the skills returned, emit one JSON report
                                  per skill on stdout, and exit 7 if any fails
                                  or 8 if any could not be fully checked within
                                  the read bounds. Use with --method skills/list
                                  or --method skills/get.
  --require-digests               With --verify: exit 9 when a skill advertises
                                  no digests (resources: "dynamic"), instead of
                                  reporting it as unverifiable and exiting 0.
  --connect-timeout <ms>          Connection timeout in ms (default 15000 for
                                  ad-hoc --server-url / target invocations; 0 =
                                  no timeout).
  --protocol-era <era>            Protocol era to negotiate: legacy, auto, or
                                  modern. Overrides the file-level protocolEra
                                  for --catalog/--config runs; ad-hoc
                                  --server-url / target runs otherwise default
                                  to legacy.
  --skill-catalog-max-skills <n>  Skills catalog budget for --verify: the most
                                  skills one run reads (positive integer;
                                  default 256). Overrides the server's
                                  skillCatalogMaxSkills in the catalog/config
                                  file.
  --skill-catalog-max-bytes <n>   Skills catalog budget for --verify: the most
                                  bytes one run reads across all skills
                                  (positive integer; default 67108864, 64 MiB).
                                  Overrides the server's skillCatalogMaxBytes in
                                  the catalog/config file.
  --format <format>               Output format: text (default; pretty-printed)
                                  or json (one JSON object on stdout, no
                                  banners).
  -q, --quiet                     Suppress everything except the result payload
                                  on stdout (or the error envelope on stderr):
                                  status lines, warnings, advisory summaries,
                                  and a stdio server's own stderr. Interactive
                                  OAuth prompts still appear when a login is
                                  needed.
  --output <path>                 Write the result to this file instead of
                                  stdout (the parent directory must exist; an
                                  existing file is replaced).
  --output-format <format>        Encoding of the --output file: json (default;
                                  the whole result, pretty-printed) or raw (the
                                  result's text, or the decoded bytes of a
                                  single image/audio/blob block). raw needs
                                  --method tools/call or resources/read.
  --tool-args-json <json>         Tool arguments as a single JSON object (e.g.
                                  '{"zip":"10001"}'). Values are passed verbatim
                                  — no key=value coercion. Mutually exclusive
                                  with --tool-arg.
  --client-config <path>          Install-level client config (default:
                                  ~/.mcp-inspector/storage/client.json, or
                                  MCP_CLIENT_CONFIG_PATH)
  --client-id <id>                OAuth client ID (static client) for HTTP
                                  servers
  --client-secret <secret>        OAuth client secret (for confidential clients)
  --client-metadata-url <url>     OAuth Client ID Metadata Document URL (CIMD)
                                  for HTTP servers
  --callback-url <url>            OAuth redirect/callback listener URL; must be
                                  loopback (default:
                                  http://127.0.0.1:6276/oauth/callback, or
                                  MCP_OAUTH_CALLBACK_URL)
  --use-stored-auth               Read the OAuth access token for --server-url
                                  from the OAuth state file (written by the web
                                  inspector) and inject it as Authorization:
                                  Bearer.
  --stored-auth-only              Never start interactive OAuth; use the shared
                                  store if present, otherwise fail with
                                  auth_required. Preferred for
                                  CI/non-interactive runs. No-op when the server
                                  does not require auth.
  --relogin                       Delete stored OAuth for this server URL from
                                  the shared store before connect (HTTP/SSE URL
                                  keys only); interactive login runs only if the
                                  server requires auth. Rejected for stdio (no
                                  URL-keyed store entry)
  --no-revoke                     Requires --relogin. Skips the RFC 7009
                                  revocation request that would otherwise end
                                  the grant at the authorization server when the
                                  local state is deleted. Also skipped when the
                                  server entry sets oauth.revokeOnClear to
                                  false.
  --wait-for-auth <sec>           Poll the OAuth state file until a token for
                                  --server-url appears (or the timeout elapses),
                                  then proceed as if --use-stored-auth were set.
                                  Use after handing off to a human to complete
                                  OAuth in a browser.
  --list-stored-auth              Print the server URLs that have a stored OAuth
                                  token (one JSON object on stdout) and exit. No
                                  server connection is made.
  --print-handoff                 Print a JSON handoff block (deepLink,
                                  portForwardCmd, oauthStatePath, apiToken) for
                                  --server-url and exit. No server connection is
                                  made.
  --completion <shell>            Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh,
                                  fish) on stdout and exit. No server connection
                                  is made.
  -h, --help                      display help for command
